findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on I/O result panics on missing file, permission error, or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a typed domain error; use map_err or ? to propagate

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on parse result panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV value aborts the program instead of yielding a typed parse error

findings.problem: as u16 — lossy cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536–4294967295 wrap to 0–65535, producing incorrect data without any error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value) and propagate the error via map_err

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() — collects all split parts into a Vec when only two fields are needed; uses split + collect instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; also masks the fact that lines with fewer than 2 fields will underflow on indexing
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to extract exactly two fields; avoid Vec allocation in the mapping closure

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line without comma panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use get(0).unwrap_or_default() or guard with a bounds check

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma-delimited field panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use get(1) or split_once(',') to safely extract the second field

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — I/O side effect inside a data-loading function that should be a pure pipeline
findings.failure_mode: hidden logging in the core contaminates purity, makes the function non-deterministic, and couples the domain to std::io
findings.fix: remove println!; move any logging to the shell layer that calls this function

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> directly instead of Result — hidden I/O with no error signal
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish success from file-missing or permission-denied; the imperative shell is not separated from the core
findings.fix: change signature to fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: Record uses String for name instead of a named newtype value object; name field is pub
findings.failure_mode: no type-level guarantee that name is non-empty or valid; raw strings leak into the domain
findings.fix: introduce a namedtype RecordName(String) with a constructor that rejects empty/whitespace-only input; make fields private or use private pub

findings.problem: value is u16 — a primitive that allows any value 0–65535 with no domain constraint
findings.failure_mode: no validation of acceptable value range; illegal values are representable
findings.fix: introduce a Value type with a fallible constructor that enforces domain bounds

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocated per line via collect() — every line heap-allocates a new Vec and String copies
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation cost per line; O(n) heap traffic for what is a simple two-field parse
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and &str slices; no Vec or String allocation needed per line

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no profiler evidence for hot-path allocation or CPU cost of load_sessions
no allocation analysis (e.g., cargo flamegraph, heaptrack) for the parsing loop
no second-ring evidence (property tests, fuzzing, or Miri) for malformed CSV handling
no CLI command evidence — this is a static review with no commands run
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate is entirely unsafe on any non-ideal input — missing file, permission denied, empty lines, lines with one field, lines with non-numeric values, and values exceeding u16 range will all panic or silently corrupt data. The functional core / imperative shell boundary is completely unestablished. A full compliant rewrite is required before this code is safe for any deployment.
